cheatsheet: Structure: Account → Property → Data stream. One property can hold multiple streams (web+app) for one unified view.
Dimensions vs. metrics: dimension = a label ('what'), metric = a number ('how much'). Every report is just the two paired up.
Key events: flagging an event as a 'key event' doesn't add tracking — it just marks it as a conversion. Old Universal Analytics name: Goal/Conversion.
Reports: Realtime = last 30 minutes (use to confirm tracking). Standard reports can take 24–48 hours to fully populate.
Segments vs. audiences: segment = one-off, lives inside Explore. Audience = reusable, persists, can drive Ads remarketing.
Scopes: every dimension/metric is scoped to user, session, or event — a mismatch is the most common cause of 'weird' numbers.
Attribution: GA4's default is Data-Driven Attribution, not last-click. Last-click overcredits closing channels; first-click overcredits discovery channels.
Campaign tracking: UTM tags identify traffic explicitly. Google Ads uses auto-tagging (gclid) instead of manual UTMs.
Advertising/budgeting: cross-channel numbers shift depending on which attribution model is applied — always say which one you're using.
Governance/cardinality: a big '(other)' row means a high-cardinality dimension, not broken tracking. Filters aren't retroactive.
BigQuery/APIs: BigQuery export is free on standard GA4 (~1M events/day cap). Data API = pull reports in code. Admin API = manage config. Measurement Protocol = send offline/server-side events.
GA4 360: Subproperty = filtered data from ONE source property (governance). Roll-up property = combines TWO+ source properties into one view.
Consent Mode: denied consent doesn't stop collection entirely — it switches GA4 to cookieless pings and modeled (estimated) data instead of full-fidelity hits.
Google Signals: only recognizes users across devices when they're signed into Google AND have Ads Personalization turned on — it's off by default and must be activated.
Setup Assistant: a checklist inside Admin, not a one-time wizard — revisit it after big changes (new streams, Ads account, key events) since it re-flags anything still incomplete.
Events: automatically collected → recommended → custom, in that priority order. Only build a custom event if no recommended event already fits — custom events skip most standard reports.
Enhanced measurement: one toggle per web stream auto-fires scroll, outbound click, site search, form interaction, video engagement, and file download events — zero code required.
DebugView: real-time event verification tool. Only shows devices explicitly flagged for debug mode — normal production traffic never appears here.
User-ID: your own logged-in identifier, sent deliberately with events, for cross-device stitching — different from (and more reliable than) Google Signals, but requires implementation work.
Cross-domain measurement: without listing both domains in tag settings, crossing to a second domain (e.g. checkout) starts a brand-new session instead of continuing the same one.
Predictive metrics: purchase probability, churn probability, predicted revenue — only available once a property has enough qualifying positive/negative examples in the past 28 days.
Custom channel groups: up to 3 channel groups per property (including Default), one marked Primary — custom groups let you define business-specific channel logic.
gtag.js vs. GTM: both install the same underlying Google tag — gtag.js is a direct code snippet, GTM is a managed container for handling many tags without further code deploys.
